title: Can Your ₹4.5 Crore Corpus Generate ₹4 Lakh a Month? Decoding Retirement Math
description: A ₹4.5 crore retirement corpus can potentially generate an initial income of ₹4 lakh per month, but sustainability depends on several factors. Systematic With.

faq.q: What is a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP)?
faq.a: An SWP allows you to withdraw a fixed amount or a fixed number of units from your mutual fund scheme at regular intervals, providing a steady income stream.

faq.q: How is income from an SWP taxed?
faq.a: Income from SWPs is taxed as capital gains. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) rules apply depending on the holding period and the type of mutual fund (equity or debt-oriented).

faq.q: Can ₹4.5 crore really provide ₹4 lakh per month sustainably?
faq.a: While it can provide ₹4 lakh per month *initially*, sustaining this for a long retirement, especially with inflation-adjusted increases, is challenging with typical investment returns and withdrawal rates. It represents a very high withdrawal rate.

faq.q: How does inflation affect my retirement corpus?
faq.a: Inflation erodes the purchasing power of your money, meaning your fixed monthly income will buy less over time. Your corpus needs to grow sufficiently to allow for inflation-adjusted withdrawals.

faq.q: What is a "safe withdrawal rate" for retirement?
faq.a: A safe withdrawal rate is the percentage of your initial corpus you can withdraw annually without running out of money. While a 4% rule is often cited internationally, Indian conditions may necessitate adjustments, typically in the 4-6% range for long-term sustainability.

faq.q: Are there alternatives to SWPs for retirement income?
faq.a: Yes, other options include interest from fixed deposits, rental income, annuity plans, and income from the National Pension System (NPS), each with its own tax implications and risk profile.

faq.q: Should I consider debt or equity funds for my retirement corpus withdrawals?
faq.a: A balanced approach is often recommended. Equity funds offer growth potential to combat inflation, while debt funds provide stability. The ideal allocation depends on your risk tolerance and time horizon.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of retirement planning in India, particularly regarding SWPs and their tax implications, but some tax rates and exemption limits cited are outdated based on recent budget changes.

corrections.note: Corrected tax rates for equity and debt mutual fund capital gains, and clarified NPS withdrawal rules based on recent amendments.

edits.why: LTCG exemption limit and tax rate for equity mutual funds were updated in Union Budget 2024.
STCG tax rate for equity-oriented funds was updated in Finance (No. 2) Act 2024.
Tax rules for debt mutual funds changed for units purchased on or after April 1, 2023.
NPS withdrawal rules for smaller corpus amounts and the taxability of the 60% lump sum were clarified.
